summary.headline: Unimech to acquire Hobel Bellows for about INR450 crore EV, all-cash from internal funds, at roughly 7x EV/EBITDA on ~INR129 crore FY26 revenue and >50% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Unimech announced the acquisition of Hobel Bellows, a metallic bellows and precision assemblies maker, via a subsidiary, for about INR450 crore EV on an all-cash basis funded from internal balance sheet cash. Management said Hobel reported about INR129 crore revenue for FY26 with EBITDA margin above 50%, and projected 15-17% growth over 3-4 years on existing customers without new-customer wins. Management said the core business saw demand recovery and better Q4 FY26 momentum, and that the FTWZ facility awaits only customs clearance, expected by end-May 2026. Q&A centred on customer concentration (two OEM groups ~93% of revenue), valuation rationale, NPCIL and AS9100 certification timelines, and capacity utilisation of 50-60%.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows - metallic bellows
segments.commentary: Over 75% of Hobel revenue per management; bellows range 2 to 16 inches, 500 g to 330 kg, for engines of 900 to 9,000 BHP. About 70% of products are single-source.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows - exhaust manifolds and structural components
segments.commentary: Remainder of revenue (under 25%) per management; margins said to be similar to bellows.

segments.name: Unimech core business
segments.commentary: Management said demand is normalising after a muted prior year, with improved momentum in Q4 FY26 and a healthy order book; no quantified figures given.

guidance_outlook: Management guides 15-17% growth over the next 3-4 years for Hobel, described as conservative and excluding new customers.
Synergies expected mainly on revenue (cross-selling, nuclear, marine/naval, aerospace), not cost; cost optimisation described as limited.
No new borrowings planned; no major capex expected near term beyond maintenance, with capex deferred until utilisation reaches 80-90%.
FTWZ facility: all approvals received, only customs clearance pending, expected by end-May 2026; delayed versus earlier timelines.
NPCIL qualification expected in about one year; AS9100 certification needed before aerospace work, timing not specified.
Payback on the acquisition estimated at 8-10 years (initial calculation).
capex_capacity: Hobel operates from a 200,000 sq ft facility plus 20,000 sq ft warehouse in Visakhapatnam SEZ; current utilisation 50-60%.
Management targets 85-90% utilisation before deploying new capex; automation and robotics expected to lift effective capacity.
Unimech had planned about INR100 crore capex for metal forming, tube bending and sheet metal; acquisition used instead.
Recent machinery additions include FANUC welding robots, seam welders, automated underwater leak test machine and 3D printer; some yet to be commissioned.
Management said no additional capex needed for AS9100 certification.
demand_pricing: Management cites a global metallic bellows addressable market of about $2.6 billion growing ~6% annually.
Two OEM groups contribute ~93% of Hobel revenue; end uses include power generation, locomotive engines, automotive and industrial systems; exports ~90%.
Cummins QSK95 gensets are an end use; Hobel's wallet share with Cummins described as small.
Margins attributed to high entry barriers, long qualification cycles, proprietary drawings and pricing power rather than cost; previous competitors were European and American.
Management says it will not sacrifice margins for growth, including avoiding automotive volume segments.
Aerospace and semiconductor customers have shown initial interest in tube bending and metal forming capabilities; no quantified pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the seller exiting at ~7x EV/EBITDA when peers trade at 25-30x?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the promoter had no succession plan (daughters settled abroad) and had crossed retirement age, so wanted an exit to a suitable buyer.

qa_highlights.question: What is client concentration and working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: Two OEM groups contribute ~93% of revenue across 10-12 geographies; about INR60 crore working capital retained and monthly cash generation said to be sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CCD a dilution risk and what are its terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the CCD is an internal instrument between holding and subsidiary, with no near-term intent to convert and negligible interest; the transaction is all cash apart from a 10% holdback for one year.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be amortisation or goodwill?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no amortisation because the investment is in a subsidiary; fixed assets are small and the deal is capability-led and asset-light.

qa_highlights.question: Can Hobel supply NPCIL reactor-island components such as expansion joints?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hobel is not NPCIL certified; qualification is needed, taking about a year, and tubular assemblies are the target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between bellows and manifolds, and by industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Bellows over 75%, with manifolds and other structural components the rest; industry-level split not available and to be taken offline.

risks_watch: Customer concentration: two OEM groups ~93% of revenue, with a single-source product base.
Execution risk on FTWZ customs clearance (expected end-May 2026) after prior delays.
Aerospace and nuclear expansion depends on AS9100 and NPCIL qualification, with timelines of roughly one year or more.
Growth guidance (15-17%) is below the analyst view of 10% standalone CAGR being conservative and Cummins-linked demand; watch actual growth.
Retention of senior and technical staff at Hobel, with compensation benchmarking and ESOPs planned over the medium term.
Integration of metal forming and tube bending operations, which stay at the Hobel facility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic and margin story, but guarded on growth and certification timelines. Management was non-committal on aggressive growth targets, NPCIL, and the CCD, and deferred several detailed questions (installed capacity, industry split) offline.
key_quotes: This debt-free business acquisition is margin accretive with strong annual cash generation, enhancing the overall quality of Unimech's earnings profile.
So instead of taking, you know, 18 to 24 months to build this organically, we now get immediate access to those opportunities.

The intent for the first 12 months or the short term I should say will always be a slow moving, but eventually when the synergies are going to catch up, so over a medium term you will see the growth coming up.
So it's basically exhaust systems, fuel lines in a high temperature are some of the applications in the aerospace.

financial_highlights.metric: Post-acquisition EBITDA return on INR450 crore

adds.what: FANUC welding robots, seam welders, automated underwater leak test machine and 3D printer (recent machinery additions, some yet to be commissioned)
FTWZ facility at Hobel (awaiting customs clearance, expected end-May 2026)

growth.why: Hobel guided to 15-17% growth over 3-4 years (midpoint 16%) on existing customers, backed by an INR65 crore+ six-month order book and 50-60% utilisation with no major capex needed near term; core Unimech demand improved in Q4 FY26 but was not quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Hobel already runs EBITDA margins above 50% (gross margin slightly below 70%) and management says it will not sacrifice margins for growth, but cost optimisation is described as limited and synergies are revenue-led.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Hobel utilisation is 50-60% with 200,000 sq ft facility, so no new capacity is needed near term; new capacity is only likely once utilisation nears the 85-90% target, and FTWZ customs clearance (expected end-May 2026) plus AS9100 and NPCIL qualifications (about a year) could add capability within 2-4 quarters.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Hobel guided 15-17% growth over 3-4 years (midpoint 16%) on existing customers, backed by an INR65 crore+ six-month order book and 50-60% utilisation with headroom.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 50-60% is well below the 80-90% trigger management set, the INR100 crore metal-forming capex was replaced by the acquisition, and management said only maintenance capex is needed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Core Unimech momentum improved in Q4 FY26 on a healthy order book and Hobel has an INR65 crore+ six-month order book, but the core improvement was not quantified.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FTWZ customs clearance has already slipped versus earlier timelines and NPCIL/AS9100 timelines run about a year, while the analyst view of 10% standalone CAGR sits below the 15-17% guide.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aerospace and semiconductor customers have shown initial interest in tube bending and metal forming, but there is no quantified pipeline and AS9100 is needed before aerospace work.

rows.label: FTWZ customs clearance at Hobel
rows.why: All approvals received and only customs clearance pending, expected by end-May 2026, though this is already delayed versus earlier timelines.

rows.label: NPCIL qualification for Hobel
rows.when: in about one year (around Q2 FY28)
rows.why: Management expects NPCIL qualification in about one year, and Hobel is not NPCIL certified today, so nuclear revenue is a 4-quarter-plus story.

rows.label: AS9100 certification
rows.why: Needed before aerospace work and no additional capex is required, but no date was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the margin and strategic story and the 15-17% Hobel growth guide, but guarded on NPCIL, AS9100 and CCD questions; analysts probed customer concentration (93% from two OEM groups), the 7x valuation versus peers and whether 15-17% growth is conservative.
